sanskrit.deva:
कस्यैष मौनः कतरन्नु मौनं प्रब्रूहि विद्वन्निह मौनभावम् ।
मौनेन विद्वानुपयाति मौनं कथं मुने मौनमिहाचरन्ति ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kasyaiṣa maunaḥ kataran nu maunaṃ prabrūhi vidvann iha maunabhāvam |
maunena vidvān upayāti maunaṃ kathaṃ mune maunam ihācaranti || 1 ||

lines.iast: kasyaiṣa maunaḥ kataran nu maunaṃ prabrūhi vidvann iha maunabhāvam
lines.deva: कस्यैष मौनः कतरन्नु मौनं प्रब्रूहि विद्वन्निह मौनभावम्

lines.iast: maunena vidvān upayāti maunaṃ kathaṃ mune maunam ihācaranti
lines.deva: मौनेन विद्वानुपयाति मौनं कथं मुने मौनमिहाचरन्ति

padaccheda.iast: kasya eṣaḥ maunaḥ kataran nu maunam prabrūhi vidvan iha mauna-bhāvam maunena vidvān upayāti maunam katham mune maunam iha ācaranti
padaccheda.deva: कस्य एषः मौनः कतरन् नु मौनम् प्रब्रूहि विद्वन् इह मौन-भावम् मौनेन विद्वान् उपयाति मौनम् कथम् मुने मौनम् इह आचरन्ति

translations.text: Of what (kind of man) is this silence? And which of the two is silence? Declare here, O wise one, the nature of silence. Does the wise man reach silence (Brahman) by silence (by keeping still)? How, O sage, do they practise silence here?

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: Dhṛtarāṣṭra speaks having heard the greatness of silence shown in the verse beginning ‘ayaṃ mānasya’ (1.41).

Śaṅkara: kasya: of what kind of man is this silence spoken of before, whose mark is the ceasing of speech and the rest? kataran nu: which of these two, not speaking or the nature of the Self, is silence? maunabhāva: the nature of silence. Does the wise man reach silence, that is Brahman, by silence, that is by keeping still, or by something else?
The edition: the visarga of maunaḥ prints as a single dot, and vidvan without its virāma (p. 237).

sanskrit.deva:
यतो न वेदा मनसा सहैनमनुप्रविशन्ति ततोऽथ मौनम् ।
यत्रोत्थितो वेदशब्दस्तथायं स तन्मयत्वेन विभाति राजन् ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yato na vedā manasā sahainam anupraviśanti tato 'tha maunam |
yatrotthito vedaśabdas tathāyaṃ sa tanmayatvena vibhāti rājan || 2 ||

lines.iast: yato na vedā manasā sahainam anupraviśanti tato 'tha maunam
lines.deva: यतो न वेदा मनसा सहैनमनुप्रविशन्ति ततोऽथ मौनम्

lines.iast: yatrotthito vedaśabdas tathāyaṃ sa tanmayatvena vibhāti rājan
lines.deva: यत्रोत्थितो वेदशब्दस्तथायं स तन्मयत्वेन विभाति राजन्

padaccheda.iast: yataḥ na vedāḥ manasā saha enam anupraviśanti tataḥ atha maunam yatra utthitaḥ veda-śabdaḥ tathā ayam saḥ tat-mayatvena vibhāti rājan
padaccheda.deva: यतः न वेदाः मनसा सह एनम् अनुप्रविशन्ति ततः अथ मौनम् यत्र उत्थितः वेद-शब्दः तथा अयम् सः तत्-मयत्वेन विभाति राजन्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Since the Vedas, together with the mind, do not enter this (Supreme Self), therefore (he) is silence. That for which the word of the Veda has arisen, such is this (Self); he shines, O king, as made of that (light).

notes: Śaṅkara: since the Vedas with the mind do not enter this Supreme Self (Taittirīya 2.4: ‘from which words turn back, not reaching it, with the mind’), for that very reason the Supreme Self, beyond the reach of speech, is silence. What then is his mark? yatra utthito vedaśabdaḥ: the object for whose sake the word of the Veda arose, that is, Brahman, the cause of the scripture and the rest; or: that which is called knowing (saṃvedana), for which the word ‘veda’ is used as its name; so this Supreme Self, taught by the word ‘veda’, is of the nature of consciousness. If he is beyond speech, how is he known to be consciousness? He shines to us as made of that, that is, as made of light: such is our own experience; there is no room for distrust. Or: in śruti, smṛti, the itihāsas and the purāṇas he is known as made of light (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.16 ‘him the gods (worship) as the light of lights’; Muṇḍaka 3.1.5 ‘made of light, bright, within the body, whom the renouncers see, their faults destroyed’; Gītā 13.17 ‘that is the light even of lights, beyond darkness’).

sanskrit.deva:
ऋचो यजूंष्यधीते यः सामवेदं च यो द्विजः ।
पापानि कुर्वन्पापेन लिप्यते न स लिप्यते ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ṛco yajūṃṣy adhīte yaḥ sāmavedaṃ ca yo dvijaḥ |
pāpāni kurvan pāpena lipyate na sa lipyate || 3 ||

lines.iast: ṛco yajūṃṣy adhīte yaḥ sāmavedaṃ ca yo dvijaḥ
lines.deva: ऋचो यजूंष्यधीते यः सामवेदं च यो द्विजः

lines.iast: pāpāni kurvan pāpena lipyate na sa lipyate
lines.deva: पापानि कुर्वन्पापेन लिप्यते न स लिप्यते

padaccheda.iast: ṛcaḥ yajūṃṣi adhīte yaḥ sāma-vedam ca yaḥ dvijaḥ pāpāni kurvan pāpena lipyate na saḥ lipyate
padaccheda.deva: ऋचः यजूंषि अधीते यः साम-वेदम् च यः द्विजः पापानि कुर्वन् पापेन लिप्यते न सः लिप्यते

translations.text: The twice-born who studies the Ṛc verses, the Yajus formulas and the Sāmaveda while committing sins: is he stained by sin, or is he not stained?

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: Dhṛtarāṣṭra speaks to learn the nature of the Veda.
Śaṅkara: he who studies the Ṛgveda and the others while committing sins: is he purified by that study of the Veda or not? ‘Tell me this’ is the intent.
The edition: the second lipyate prints like lipyane (the letters ‘ta’ and ‘na’ look alike in this type, p. 239); read lipyate from the sense and the first verb.

sanskrit.deva:
नैनं सामान्यृचो वापि यजूंषि च विचक्षण ।
त्रायन्ते कर्मणः पापान्न ते मिथ्या ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nainaṃ sāmāny ṛco vāpi yajūṃṣi ca vicakṣaṇa |
trāyante karmaṇaḥ pāpān na te mithyā bravīmy aham || 4 ||

lines.iast: nainaṃ sāmāny ṛco vāpi yajūṃṣi ca vicakṣaṇa
lines.deva: नैनं सामान्यृचो वापि यजूंषि च विचक्षण

lines.iast: trāyante karmaṇaḥ pāpān na te mithyā bravīmy aham
lines.deva: त्रायन्ते कर्मणः पापान्न ते मिथ्या ब्रवीम्यहम्

padaccheda.iast: na enam sāmāni ṛcaḥ vā api yajūṃṣi ca vicakṣaṇa trāyante karmaṇaḥ pāpāt na te mithyā bravīmi aham
padaccheda.deva: न एनम् सामानि ऋचः वा अपि यजूंषि च विचक्षण त्रायन्ते कर्मणः पापात् न ते मिथ्या ब्रवीमि अहम्

translations.text: Neither the Sāman chants nor the Ṛc verses nor the Yajus formulas, O discerning one, protect him (who does what is forbidden) from sinful action. I do not speak falsely to you.

notes: Śaṅkara: him who studies the Ṛgveda and the others while committing sins, who does what is forbidden, the Vedas do not protect from sinful action. ‘I do not speak falsely to you’: it is just so; there is no room for distrust here.

sanskrit.deva:
न च्छन्दांसि वृजिनात्तारयन्ति मायाविनं मायया वर्तमानम् ।
नीडं शकुन्ता इव जातपक्षाश्छन्दांस्येनं प्रजहन्त्यन्तकाले ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na cchandāṃsi vṛjināt tārayanti māyāvinaṃ māyayā vartamānam |
nīḍaṃ śakuntā iva jātapakṣāś chandāṃsy enaṃ prajahanty antakāle || 5 ||

lines.iast: na cchandāṃsi vṛjināt tārayanti māyāvinaṃ māyayā vartamānam
lines.deva: न च्छन्दांसि वृजिनात्तारयन्ति मायाविनं मायया वर्तमानम्

lines.iast: nīḍaṃ śakuntā iva jātapakṣāś chandāṃsy enaṃ prajahanty antakāle

padaccheda.iast: na chandāṃsi vṛjināt tārayanti māyāvinam māyayā vartamānam nīḍam śakuntāḥ iva jāta-pakṣāḥ chandāṃsi enam prajahanti anta-kāle
padaccheda.deva: न छन्दांसि वृजिनात् तारयन्ति मायाविनम् मायया वर्तमानम् नीडम् शकुन्ताः इव जात-पक्षाः छन्दांसि एनम् प्रजहन्ति अन्त-काले

words.meaning: at the time of the end

translations.text: The Vedas do not carry across from wrong the deceitful man (who has studied them) and lives by deceit. As birds whose wings have grown leave the nest, the Vedas leave him at the time of death.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: ‘what do they do, then?’ To this he says:

Śaṅkara: the Vedas do not carry across, do not protect, from wrong, that is adharma, this man who denies (the next world), a doer of sin, who has studied the Veda and its sense, the deceitful man (māyāvin), one who makes a banner of dharma, living by deceit, that is, whose conduct is false. What will they do? As birds whose wings have grown leave the nest, their own support, so the Vedas at the time of the end, the time of death, leave him who was their support: they do not serve the end of man.
The edition: in the bhāṣya māyāvinaṃ prints māyākinaṃ (p. 240).

sanskrit.deva:
न चेद्वेदा वेदविदं त्रातुं शक्ता विचक्षण ।
अथ कस्मात्प्रलापोऽयं ब्राह्मणानां सनातनः ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na ced vedā vedavidaṃ trātuṃ śaktā vicakṣaṇa |
atha kasmāt pralāpo 'yaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ sanātanaḥ || 6 ||

lines.iast: na ced vedā vedavidaṃ trātuṃ śaktā vicakṣaṇa
lines.deva: न चेद्वेदा वेदविदं त्रातुं शक्ता विचक्षण

lines.iast: atha kasmāt pralāpo 'yaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ sanātanaḥ

padaccheda.iast: na cet vedāḥ veda-vidam trātum śaktāḥ vicakṣaṇa atha kasmāt pralāpaḥ ayam brāhmaṇānām sanātanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: न चेत् वेदाः वेद-विदम् त्रातुम् शक्ताः विचक्षण अथ कस्मात् प्रलापः अयम् ब्राह्मणानाम् सनातनः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: If the Vedas cannot protect the knower of the Veda, O discerning one, why then this age-old talk of the brahmins?

notes: Śaṅkara: in the verses beginning ‘karmodaye’ (1.9) the obligatory rites and those prompted by desire were shown to be causes of reaching the world of the fathers and the like, and so causes of the evil of saṃsāra, and forbidden action to be a cause of hell. If then the Vedas cannot protect the knower of the Veda, for what reason is there this age-old (sanātana, long-standing) talk? The sense: the study of the Veda, inquiry into its meaning and the doing of what it enjoins would then not be things to be done, being causes of the evil of saṃsāra.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्यैव नामादिविशेषरूपैरिदं जगद्भाति महानुभाव ।
निर्दिश्य सम्यक्प्रवदन्ति वेदास्तद्विश्ववैरूप्यमुदाहरन्ति ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasyaiva nāmādiviśeṣarūpair idaṃ jagad bhāti mahānubhāva |
nirdiśya samyak pravadanti vedās tad viśvavairūpyam udāharanti || 7 ||

lines.iast: tasyaiva nāmādiviśeṣarūpair idaṃ jagad bhāti mahānubhāva
nirdiśya samyak pravadanti vedās tad viśvavairūpyam udāharanti

padaccheda.iast: tasya eva nāma-ādi-viśeṣa-rūpaiḥ idam jagat bhāti mahā-anubhāva nirdiśya samyak pravadanti vedāḥ tat viśva-vairūpyam udāharanti
padaccheda.deva: तस्य एव नाम-आदि-विशेष-रूपैः इदम् जगत् भाति महा-अनुभाव निर्दिश्य सम्यक् प्रवदन्ति वेदाः तत् विश्व-वैरूप्यम् उदाहरन्ति

words.meaning: by the particular forms, name and the rest
unlike the form of the universe

translations.text: By the particular forms, name and the rest, of him alone this world appears, O noble one. Having pointed this out, the Vedas declare (his) true (form); (the sages too) describe that (Brahman) as unlike the form of the universe.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing verses 7–9: the talk would be idle if this were the sense of the Veda; but the sense of the Veda is another, liberation, the highest human end, beyond heaven and the like. Rites and meditations are taught by the Veda because they are of use to man step by step: they purify the inner organ, which serves knowledge, the means of reaching liberation. So the Veda shows the Supreme Self as the highest end: it shows that the worlds of heaven are not the end of man and are joyless, the lot of the ignorant (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.11 ‘joyless are those worlds, covered by blind darkness’); that the knower of the Self has done all there is to do (4.4.12 ‘if a man should know the Self as “I am this”, wishing what, for whose desire, should he suffer after the body?’); that the knower of the Self reaches deathlessness and the one who does not know it perishes and meets evil (4.4.14 ‘while we are here we may know it; if not, great is the loss’); and with passages such as 4.4.15 (‘when one sees him directly as the Self, the god, lord of what was and will be, one shrinks from nothing’) it shows again and again his nature, the seeing of him and its fruit. Then, as if thinking ‘how shall I free this sinner, dragged this way and that by passion and the rest as by crocodiles, overcome by objects, and set him in the highest place, the Supreme Self, full bliss, self-rule, called liberation?’, it applies sacrifice and the rest as means to the desire to know, which leads to knowledge, the means of reaching it (4.4.22 ‘him the brahmins seek to know by the recitation of the Veda, by sacrifice, by giving, by austerity, by fasting’). So sacrifice and the rest are of use to man only as serving that; directed to heaven and the like they are of no more use than the śyena rite, being causes of the evil of saṃsāra (Muṇḍaka 1.2.7 ‘unsteady boats are these forms of sacrifice … the fools who delight in this as the good go again to old age and death’). Since the Vedas, teaching liberation and its means, put an end to the evil of saṃsāra, they can protect the knower of the Veda: with all this in mind he speaks three verses, and in the first shows the Supreme Self, ever immediate, the highest human end.

Śaṅkara: by the particular forms, name and the rest, of that Supreme Self alone, imagined by māyā, this world appears. How is this known? Having pointed out the many forms made by māyā (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.5.19 ‘Indra by his powers goes in many forms’), the Vedas declare his true form (the same passage: ‘this Brahman, without before or after, without inside or outside; this Self is Brahman, perceiving all’); having pointed out with ‘there are two forms of Brahman, the formed and the formless’ (2.3.1) the world of the formed and the formless as his, they declare his true form with ‘not this, not this’; having pointed out ether and the rest down to the earth as his effect (Taittirīya 2.1), they declare his true form by way of the sheaths, ‘from which words turn back’ (2.4); having pointed out name and the rest up to prāṇa as the world caused by his māyā (Chāndogya 7.1.1 ‘teach me, sir’), they declare his true form, the plenitude beyond darkness standing in its own greatness (7.24.1 ‘where one sees nothing else … that is the plenitude’). Not the Vedas alone: the sages too describe that Brahman as viśvavairūpya, of a form contrary to the form of the universe (Parāśara, Viṣṇu Purāṇa 6.7.53–54: ‘that in which all difference has set, mere being, beyond the reach of the mind, known by the self, is the knowledge called Brahman; and that is the highest form of Viṣṇu, called the formless, … marked by being unlike the form of the universe’).

sanskrit.deva:
तदर्थमुक्तं तप एतदिज्या ताभ्यामसौ पुण्यमुपैति विद्वान् ।
पुण्येन पापं विनिहत्य पश्चात्स जायते ज्ञानविदीपितात्मा ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tadartham uktaṃ tapa etad ijyā tābhyām asau puṇyam upaiti vidvān |
puṇyena pāpaṃ vinihatya paścāt sa jāyate jñānavidīpitātmā || 8 ||

lines.iast: tadartham uktaṃ tapa etad ijyā tābhyām asau puṇyam upaiti vidvān
lines.deva: तदर्थमुक्तं तप एतदिज्या ताभ्यामसौ पुण्यमुपैति विद्वान्

lines.iast: puṇyena pāpaṃ vinihatya paścāt sa jāyate jñānavidīpitātmā
lines.deva: पुण्येन पापं विनिहत्य पश्चात्स जायते ज्ञानविदीपितात्मा

padaccheda.iast: tat-artham uktam tapaḥ etat ijyā tābhyām asau puṇyam upaiti vidvān puṇyena pāpam vinihatya paścāt saḥ jāyate jñāna-vidīpita-ātmā
padaccheda.deva: तत्-अर्थम् उक्तम् तपः एतत् इज्या ताभ्याम् असौ पुण्यम् उपैति विद्वान् पुण्येन पापम् विनिहत्य पश्चात् सः जायते ज्ञान-विदीपित-आत्मा

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

words.meaning: one whose self is lit up by knowledge

translations.text: For the sake of that (Brahman) this austerity and sacrifice are taught. By these two the knowing man (who does them for the Lord) gains merit; having destroyed sin by merit, he afterwards becomes one whose self is lit up by knowledge.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing verses 8–9: now he shows in two verses that rites done for the Lord are of use to man step by step, through the purity that knowledge, the means of reaching him, requires; and that the others, being causes of the evil of saṃsāra, are of no use to man.

Śaṅkara: for the sake of that Brahman whose form is contrary to the form of the universe the Veda teaches austerity, the kṛcchra, the cāndrāyaṇa and the like, and sacrifice, the jyotiṣṭoma and the like. By these two the knowing man, who knows the application just stated and does the rites for the Lord, gains merit, that is, is joined with the unseen result (apūrva) born of the rite. Having destroyed sin by that merit, afterwards, all his taint destroyed, he becomes one whose self is lit up by knowledge: his own nature, Brahman, consciousness, being and bliss, without a second, is revealed by knowledge.
The edition: the verse is unnumbered (p. 244), and at reduced size ta- prints like na- (tābhyām, jāyate).

sanskrit.deva:
ज्ञानेन चात्मानमुपैति विद्वान्न चान्यथा वर्गफलानुकाङ्क्षी ।
अस्मिन्कृतं तत्परिगृह्य सर्वममुत्र भुङ्क्ते पुनरेति मार्गम् ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
jñānena cātmānam upaiti vidvān na cānyathā vargaphalānukāṅkṣī |
asmin kṛtaṃ tat parigṛhya sarvam amutra bhuṅkte punar eti mārgam || 9 ||

lines.iast: jñānena cātmānam upaiti vidvān na cānyathā vargaphalānukāṅkṣī
asmin kṛtaṃ tat parigṛhya sarvam amutra bhuṅkte punar eti mārgam
lines.deva: अस्मिन्कृतं तत्परिगृह्य सर्वममुत्र भुङ्क्ते पुनरेति मार्गम्

padaccheda.iast: jñānena ca ātmānam upaiti vidvān na ca anyathā varga-phala-anukāṅkṣī asmin kṛtam tat parigṛhya sarvam amutra bhuṅkte punaḥ eti mārgam
padaccheda.deva: ज्ञानेन च आत्मानम् उपैति विद्वान् न च अन्यथा वर्ग-फल-अनुकाङ्क्षी अस्मिन् कृतम् तत् परिगृह्य सर्वम् अमुत्र भुङ्क्ते पुनः एति मार्गम्

words.meaning: longing for the fruits of the group (of senses)

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.

translations.text: And by knowledge the knower reaches the Self, not otherwise. (Otherwise), longing for the fruits of the senses, he takes all that he did in this world, enjoys (its fruit) in the other, and comes again to the path (of saṃsāra).

notes: Śaṅkara: by knowledge the knower of the Self reaches the Supreme Self. Otherwise, not doing action for the Lord, his taint not wholly destroyed, he does not become a knower. Then, longing for the fruits of the group, that is, the fruits of the senses, heaven and the like, he takes all that he did in this world, sacrifice and the rest, and enjoys its fruit in the other world; then by the remainder of his action he comes again to the path, the path of saṃsāra (Chāndogya 5.10.5 ‘having dwelt there as long as the remainder lasts, they return by this same way’).
The edition: the anusvāra of mārgaṃ is not clear in the bhāṣya (p. 245).

sanskrit.deva:
अस्मिꣳल्लोके तपस्तप्तं फलमन्यत्र भुज्यते ।
ब्राह्मणानां तपः स्वृद्धमन्येषां तावदेव तत् ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
asmim̐l loke tapas taptaṃ phalam anyatra bhujyate |
brāhmaṇānāṃ tapaḥ svṛddham anyeṣāṃ tāvad eva tat || 10 ||

lines.iast: asmim̐l loke tapas taptaṃ phalam anyatra bhujyate
brāhmaṇānāṃ tapaḥ svṛddham anyeṣāṃ tāvad eva tat

padaccheda.iast: asmin loke tapaḥ taptam phalam anyatra bhujyate brāhmaṇānām tapaḥ svṛddham anyeṣām tāvat eva tat
padaccheda.deva: अस्मिन् लोके तपः तप्तम् फलम् अन्यत्र भुज्यते ब्राह्मणानाम् तपः स्वृद्धम् अन्येषाम् तावत् एव तत्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Of the austerity practised in this world the fruit is enjoyed elsewhere. The austerity of brahmins (who know Brahman) is richly prosperous; that of others is only so much.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now he states the difference in the fruit of actions as they are done by the knower and the one who does not know.

Śaṅkara: the fruit of austerity practised in this world is enjoyed in the other: so much is common to all. For brahmins, the knowers of Brahman, there is this difference: their austerity becomes exceedingly rich, a cause of increase in the fruit (Chāndogya 1.1.10 ‘what one does with knowledge, with faith, with the Upaniṣad, that becomes the more powerful’). For others, who do not know the Self and are given to objects, it is only so much: not enriched, it is the means only to the fruit heard of for that act, not a cause of its increase.
The edition: verses 10–11 are unnumbered (p. 246).

sanskrit.deva:
कथं समृद्धमत्यर्थं तपो भवति केवलम् ।
सनत्सुजात तद्ब्रूहि कथं विद्यामहं प्रभो ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kathaṃ samṛddham atyarthaṃ tapo bhavati kevalam |
sanatsujāta tad brūhi kathaṃ vidyām ahaṃ prabho || 11 ||

padaccheda.deva: कथम् समृद्धम् अत्यर्थम् तपः भवति केवलम् सनत्सुजात तत् ब्रूहि कथम् विद्याम् अहम् प्रभो

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: How does austerity become exceedingly prosperous, and alone (kevala)? Tell that, O Sanatsujāta: how may I know it, O lord?

notes: Śaṅkara: the verse is plain.

sanskrit.deva:
निष्कल्मषं तपस्त्वेतत्केवलं परिचक्षते ।
एतत्समृद्धमत्यर्थं तपो भवति नान्यथा ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
niṣkalmaṣaṃ tapas tv etat kevalaṃ paricakṣate |
etat samṛddham atyarthaṃ tapo bhavati nānyathā || 12 ||

lines.iast: niṣkalmaṣaṃ tapas tv etat kevalaṃ paricakṣate
etat samṛddham atyarthaṃ tapo bhavati nānyathā

padaccheda.iast: niṣkalmaṣam tapaḥ tu etat kevalam paricakṣate etat samṛddham atyartham tapaḥ bhavati na anyathā
padaccheda.deva: निष्कल्मषम् तपः तु एतत् केवलम् परिचक्षते एतत् समृद्धम् अत्यर्थम् तपः भवति न अन्यथा

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: This austerity that is stainless they call alone (kevala, the seed of all). This austerity becomes exceedingly prosperous, not otherwise.

notes: Śaṅkara: the austerity that is stainless they call kevala; kevala is said to be the seed: what is the seed, the cause, of this whole manifold is called kevala. So Uśanas says: ‘the principle that stands in the balance of the guṇas is called kevala; from kevala arose this world of being and non-being’. This alone is the kevala austerity, and it becomes exceedingly prosperous, not otherwise: when it is not stainless but stained, it does not become exceedingly prosperous.

sanskrit.deva:
तपोमूलमिदं सर्वं यन्मां पृच्छसि क्षत्रिय ।
तपसा वेदविद्वांसः परं त्वमृतमाप्नुयुः ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tapomūlam idaṃ sarvaṃ yan māṃ pṛcchasi kṣatriya |
tapasā vedavidvāṃsaḥ paraṃ tv amṛtam āpnuyuḥ || 13 ||

padaccheda.deva: तपः-मूलम् इदम् सर्वम् यत् माम् पृच्छसि क्षत्रिय तपसा वेद-विद्वांसः परम् तु अमृतम् आप्नुयुः

translations.text: All this that you ask me about is rooted in austerity, O warrior. By austerity those learned in the Veda reach the supreme deathlessness.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he praises this (stainless austerity). On the verse itself: its sense is plain.

sanskrit.deva:
कल्मषं तपसो ब्रूहि श्रुतं निष्कल्मषं तपः ।
सनत्सुजात येनेदं विद्यां गुह्यं सनातनम् ॥ १४ ॥

kalmaṣaṃ tapaso brūhi śrutaṃ niṣkalmaṣaṃ tapaḥ |
sanatsujāta yenedaṃ vidyāṃ guhyaṃ sanātanam || 14 ||

lines.iast: kalmaṣaṃ tapaso brūhi śrutaṃ niṣkalmaṣaṃ tapaḥ
lines.deva: कल्मषं तपसो ब्रूहि श्रुतं निष्कल्मषं तपः

padaccheda.iast: kalmaṣam tapasaḥ brūhi śrutam niṣkalmaṣam tapaḥ sanatsujāta yena idam vidyām guhyam sanātanam
padaccheda.deva: कल्मषम् तपसः ब्रूहि श्रुतम् निष्कल्मषम् तपः सनत्सुजात येन इदम् विद्याम् गुह्यम् सनातनम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Tell (me) the stain of austerity. I have heard of stainless austerity, O Sanatsujāta, by which I may know this secret, eternal (Brahman).

notes: Śaṅkara: tell the stain of the austerity heard of in ‘this stainless austerity they call kevala’ (2.12), O Sanatsujāta, by which stainless austerity I may know this Brahman, secret and eternal.

क्रोधादयो द्वादश यस्य दोषास्तथा नृशंसानि च सप्त राजन् ।
ज्ञानादयो द्वादश चाततानाः शास्त्रे गुणा ये विदिता द्विजानाम् ॥ १५ ॥

krodhādayo dvādaśa yasya doṣās tathā nṛśaṃsāni ca sapta rājan |
jñānādayo dvādaśa cātatānāḥ śāstre guṇā ye viditā dvijānām || 15 ||

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: Anger and the rest, twelve, are the faults of (that austerity), and likewise seven cruelties, O king; and knowledge and the rest, twelve, set out at length, are the virtues of the twice-born known in scripture (these I shall tell).

notes: Śaṅkara: anger and the rest, twelve, are the faults of which austerity; likewise seven cruelties, O king, are faults of that austerity; and knowledge and the rest, twelve, set out at length (vistīryamāṇa), are the virtues of the twice-born known in scripture, the scripture of the Veda. The intent: ‘these virtues and faults I shall tell’.

sanskrit.deva:
क्रोधः कामो लोभमोहौ विवित्सा कृपासूया मानशोकौ स्पृहा च ।
ईर्ष्या जुगुप्सा च महागुणेन सदा वर्ज्या द्वादशैते नरेण ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
krodhaḥ kāmo lobhamohau vivitsā kṛpāsūyā mānaśokau spṛhā ca |
īrṣyā jugupsā ca mahāguṇena sadā varjyā dvādaśaite nareṇa || 16 ||

lines.iast: krodhaḥ kāmo lobhamohau vivitsā kṛpāsūyā mānaśokau spṛhā ca
lines.deva: क्रोधः कामो लोभमोहौ विवित्सा कृपासूया मानशोकौ स्पृहा च

lines.iast: īrṣyā jugupsā ca mahāguṇena sadā varjyā dvādaśaite nareṇa
lines.deva: ईर्ष्या जुगुप्सा च महागुणेन सदा वर्ज्या द्वादशैते नरेण

padaccheda.iast: krodhaḥ kāmaḥ lobha-mohau vivitsā kṛpā asūyā māna-śokau spṛhā ca īrṣyā jugupsā ca mahā-guṇena sadā varjyāḥ dvādaśa ete nareṇa
padaccheda.deva: क्रोधः कामः लोभ-मोहौ विवित्सा कृपा असूया मान-शोकौ स्पृहा च ईर्ष्या जुगुप्सा च महा-गुणेन सदा वर्ज्याः द्वादश एते नरेण

translations.text: Anger, desire, greed and delusion, the craving (to taste objects), pitilessness, detraction, pride and grief, longing, jealousy and aversion: these twelve are always to be avoided by a man of great virtue.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he shows anger and the rest.

Śaṅkara: anger (krodha) is the disturbance of the inner organ that arises when desire is thwarted; it is the cause of striking, abuse and the like, causes the loss of what is desired, and its marks are sweating, trembling of the limbs and the like. Desire (kāma): longing for women and the like. Greed (lobha): the wish for another's wealth, and the inability to give one's own wealth to a worthy recipient. Delusion (moha): lacking discrimination between what is to be done and what is not. vivitsā: the wish to know, that is to taste, the savour of objects. akṛpā: hardness. asūyā: bringing out faults in virtues, or intolerance of others' virtues and the like. māna: thinking much of oneself. Grief (śoka): the disturbance of the inner organ born of parting from what is dear, marked by weeping, brooding and the like, about what cannot be remedied. spṛhā: the wish to enjoy objects. īrṣyā: inability to bear another's prosperity. jugupsā: the wish to conceal others' virtues, or loathing. These faults, anger and the rest, the stains of austerity, are always to be avoided by the man of great virtue, the brahmin, in whom union with high virtue is natural (Gītā 18.42 ‘calm, restraint, austerity, purity … the work of the brahmin, born of his nature’). Or: the great virtue is the virtue of reaching Brahman, and they are always to be avoided by one endowed with it (Nāmamahodadhi: ‘Brahman is called great (mahat), being greater than the great; one who has the virtue of reaching it is called mahāguṇa’).

Śaṅkara reads akṛpā (his gloss: ‘akṛpā: hardness’), taking vivitsākṛpāsūyā as vivitsā akṛpā asūyā; the edition prints vivitsā kṛpāsūyā, kept, and the word meaning gives kṛpā as printed. The twelve, as he counts them: krodha, kāma, lobha, moha, vivitsā, akṛpā, asūyā, māna, śoka, spṛhā, īrṣyā, jugupsā.
The edition: in the bhāṣya bībhatsā prints vībhatsā (p. 249).

sanskrit.deva:
एकैकमेते राजेन्द्र मनुष्यं पर्युपासते ।
लिप्समानोऽन्तरं तेषां मृगाणामिव लुब्धकः ॥ १७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ekaikam ete rājendra manuṣyaṃ paryupāsate |
lipsamāno 'ntaraṃ teṣāṃ mṛgāṇām iva lubdhakaḥ || 17 ||

lines.iast: ekaikam ete rājendra manuṣyaṃ paryupāsate
lipsamāno 'ntaraṃ teṣāṃ mṛgāṇām iva lubdhakaḥ

padaccheda.iast: ekaikam ete rāja-indra manuṣyam paryupāsate lipsamānaḥ antaram teṣām mṛgāṇām iva lubdhakaḥ
padaccheda.deva: एकैकम् एते राज-इन्द्र मनुष्यम् पर्युपासते लिप्समानः अन्तरम् तेषाम् मृगाणाम् इव लुब्धकः

translations.text: These, O lord of kings, wait upon each man, seeking an opening in them (men), as a hunter (seeks an opening) in deer.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he states the reason they are always to be avoided.

Śaṅkara: as a hunter, seeking an opening, a weak spot, in deer, intent on finding a gap, follows them, and having found the opening kills them, so these, anger and the rest, intent on finding a gap in men, wait upon each man. Or the reading is manuṣyān: then the construction is ‘they wait upon men, each one separately’. Having found the opening, they kill them. So even one of these faults is a cause of ruin, and therefore they are always to be avoided (Hairaṇyagarbha: ‘as lions, tigers, wild beasts and the like harass the traveller in the wilderness, so do anger and the other vices men’).

sanskrit.deva:
संभोगसंविद्विषमेधमानो दत्तानुतापी कृपणोऽबलीयान् ।
वर्गप्रशंसी वनितां च द्वेष्टा एते परे सप्त नृशंसरूपाः ॥ १८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
saṃbhogasaṃvid viṣamedhamāno dattānutāpī kṛpaṇo 'balīyān |
vargapraśaṃsī vanitāṃ ca dveṣṭā ete pare sapta nṛśaṃsarūpāḥ || 18 ||

lines.iast: saṃbhogasaṃvid viṣamedhamāno dattānutāpī kṛpaṇo 'balīyān
vargapraśaṃsī vanitāṃ ca dveṣṭā ete pare sapta nṛśaṃsarūpāḥ

words.meaning: who regrets what he has given

translations.text: He whose thought is on enjoyment, he who prospers (by harming others) like poison, he who regrets what he has given, the mean man, the weak (in knowledge), he who praises (the senses), and he who hates his wife: these seven others are cruel in form.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now he states the seven cruelties.

Śaṅkara: saṃbhogasaṃvit: he whose thought is on enjoyment, the enjoyment of objects. viṣam edhamānaḥ: he who grows, prospers, by doing harm to others like poison. Or the other reading is dviṣam edhamānaḥ: he who prospers by doing hateful deeds to living beings, by that very means. dattānutāpī: he who, having given wealth and the like with the thought of dharma, afterwards is pained, thinking ‘why did I give?’. kṛpaṇa: he who bears every insult out of greed for the gain of the least scrap of wealth. abalīyān: void of the strength of knowledge. vargapraśaṃsī: he who praises the group of the senses. vanitāṃ ca dveṣṭā: he who hates his wife, who has no other refuge. These seven, other than anger and the rest named before, are cruel in form.
The edition: in the bhāṣya bhāryāṃ prints without its anusvāra (p. 250).

sanskrit.deva:

sanskrit.iast:

yajñaś ca dānaṃ ca dhṛtiḥ śamaś ca mahāvratā dvādaśa brāhmaṇasya || 19 ||

lines.iast: jñānaṃ ca satyaṃ ca damaḥ śrutaṃ ca amātsaryaṃ hrīs titikṣānasūyā
lines.deva: ज्ञानं च सत्यं च दमः श्रुतं च अमात्सर्यं ह्रीस्तितिक्षानसूया

lines.iast: yajñaś ca dānaṃ ca dhṛtiḥ śamaś ca mahāvratā dvādaśa brāhmaṇasya
lines.deva: यज्ञश्च दानं च धृतिः शमश्च महाव्रता द्वादश ब्राह्मणस्य

padaccheda.deva: ज्ञानम् च सत्यम् च दमः श्रुतम् च अमात्सर्यम् ह्रीः तितिक्षा अनसूया यज्ञः च दानम् च धृतिः शमः च महा-व्रताः द्वादश ब्राह्मणस्य

translations.text: Knowledge, truth, restraint and learning, freedom from envy, shame, forbearance, freedom from detraction, sacrifice and giving, firmness and quiescence: these twelve are the great vows of the brahmin.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now the twelve virtues, knowledge and the rest, are told.

Śaṅkara: jñāna: knowing the truth of things. satya: speaking of things as they are, and the good of beings. dama: taming the mind. śruta: hearing the scripture on the Self. mātsarya: not bearing (the good of) any being; its absence is amātsarya. hrī: shame at doing what should not be done. titikṣā: bearing the pairs (of opposites). anasūyā: not bringing out the faults of others. yajña: the agniṣṭoma and the rest, and the great sacrifices. dāna: giving wealth and the like to brahmins. dhṛti: holding the senses in check even when objects are near. śama: the stilling of the inner organ; some say, of the outer organs. These twelve, knowledge and the rest, are the great vows of the brahmin, means to the highest human end.

sanskrit.deva:
यस्त्वेतेभ्योऽप्रवसेद्द्वादशभ्यः सर्वामिमां पृथिवीं स प्रशिष्यात् ।
त्रिभिर्द्वाभ्यामेकतो वा विमुक्ताः क्रमाद्विशिष्टा मौनभूता भवन्ति ॥ २० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yas tv etebhyo 'pravased dvādaśabhyaḥ sarvām imāṃ pṛthivīṃ sa praśiṣyāt |
tribhir dvābhyām ekato vā vimuktāḥ kramād viśiṣṭā maunabhūtā bhavanti || 20 ||

lines.iast: yas tv etebhyo 'pravased dvādaśabhyaḥ sarvām imāṃ pṛthivīṃ sa praśiṣyāt
tribhir dvābhyām ekato vā vimuktāḥ kramād viśiṣṭā maunabhūtā bhavanti
lines.deva: त्रिभिर्द्वाभ्यामेकतो वा विमुक्ताः क्रमाद्विशिष्टा मौनभूता भवन्ति

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ tu etebhyaḥ apravaset dvādaśabhyaḥ sarvām imām pṛthivīm saḥ praśiṣyāt tribhiḥ dvābhyām ekataḥ vā vimuktāḥ kramāt viśiṣṭāḥ mauna-bhūtāḥ bhavanti
padaccheda.deva: यः तु एतेभ्यः अप्रवसेत् द्वादशभ्यः सर्वाम् इमाम् पृथिवीम् सः प्रशिष्यात् त्रिभिः द्वाभ्याम् एकतः वा विमुक्ताः क्रमात् विशिष्टाः मौन-भूताः भवन्ति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.
past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: He who does not depart from these twelve would rule this whole earth. Those (not parted) from three, two or one (of them) become in due course distinguished (as knowers), and become silence (Brahman).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: the virtues brought forward before as ‘knowledge and the rest, twelve, set out at length’ (2.15) have been described; now he praises them.

Śaṅkara: he who does not depart from these, who stays endowed with them, rules this whole earth, makes it subject to himself. Those who are not parted (avimuktāḥ) from three, from two, or from one of these, who are endowed with even one of them, become in due course distinguished, knowers, and become silence, that is, become Brahman.
Śaṅkara reads avimuktāḥ (ekato vāvimuktāḥ); the edition prints vā vimuktāḥ, the verse letters worn (p. 252), kept, and the word meaning gives vimuktāḥ as printed. The translation follows his reading.

sanskrit.deva:
दमोऽष्टादशदोषः स्यात्प्रतिकूलं कृते भवेत् ।
अनृतं पैशुनं तृष्णा प्रातिकूल्यं तमोऽरतिः ॥ २१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
damo 'ṣṭādaśadoṣaḥ syāt pratikūlaṃ kṛte bhavet |
anṛtaṃ paiśunaṃ tṛṣṇā prātikūlyaṃ tamo 'ratiḥ || 21 ||

lines.iast: damo 'ṣṭādaśadoṣaḥ syāt pratikūlaṃ kṛte bhavet
anṛtaṃ paiśunaṃ tṛṣṇā prātikūlyaṃ tamo 'ratiḥ

padaccheda.iast: damaḥ aṣṭādaśa-doṣaḥ syāt pratikūlam kṛte bhavet anṛtam paiśunam tṛṣṇā prātikūlyam tamaḥ aratiḥ
padaccheda.deva: दमः अष्टादश-दोषः स्यात् प्रतिकूलम् कृते भवेत् अनृतम् पैशुनम् तृष्णा प्रातिकूल्यम् तमः अरतिः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. loc. sg.

translations.text: Restraint has eighteen faults: when (any one of them) is done, what is contrary (to restraint) is done. Untruth, slander, thirst, hostility, darkness (ignorance), discontent,

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing verses 21–23: now he states the faults of restraint in three verses. He comments on the three together after verse 23.

Śaṅkara: damaḥ aṣṭādaśadoṣaḥ syāt: restraint is attended by eighteen faults. Why are they its faults? When any one of them is done, what is contrary to restraint is done. Which are they? anṛta: speech not as things are. paiśuna: speech that blames others. tṛṣṇā: the wish for objects. prātikūlya: hostility to all. tamas: ignorance. arati: not being content with what comes; or (reading rati) delight in the enjoyment of women.

sanskrit.deva:
लोकद्वेषोऽभिमानश्च विवादः प्राणिपीडनम् ।
परिवादोऽतिवादश्च परितापोऽक्षमा धृतिः ॥ २२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
lokadveṣo 'bhimānaś ca vivādaḥ prāṇipīḍanam |
parivādo 'tivādaś ca paritāpo 'kṣamā dhṛtiḥ || 22 ||

lines.iast: lokadveṣo 'bhimānaś ca vivādaḥ prāṇipīḍanam
parivādo 'tivādaś ca paritāpo 'kṣamā dhṛtiḥ

padaccheda.iast: loka-dveṣaḥ abhimānaḥ ca vivādaḥ prāṇi-pīḍanam parivādaḥ ativādaḥ ca paritāpaḥ akṣamā dhṛtiḥ
padaccheda.deva: लोक-द्वेषः अभिमानः च विवादः प्राणि-पीडनम् परिवादः अतिवादः च परितापः अक्षमा धृतिः

translations.text: hatred of people and arrogance, quarrelling, harming living beings, censure and excessive talk, brooding, impatience, unsteadiness,

notes: Śaṅkara: lokadveṣa: conduct that distresses people. abhimāna: bowing to no one. vivāda: quarrelling among people. prāṇipīḍana: killing living beings to fill one's own body. parivāda: speaking ill of others to their face. ativāda: pointless, excessive chatter. paritāpa: brooding on sorrow in vain. akṣamā: not bearing the pairs (of opposites). adhṛti: restlessness among the objects of the senses.

Śaṅkara reads adhṛtiḥ (akṣamādhṛtiḥ = akṣamā adhṛtiḥ), which the count of eighteen needs; the edition prints the words spaced akṣamā dhṛtiḥ (p. 252), kept, and the word meaning gives dhṛtiḥ as printed. The translation follows his reading.

sanskrit.deva:
असिद्धिः पापकृत्यं च हिंसा चेति प्रकीर्तिताः ।
एतैर्दोषैर्विमुक्तो यः स दमः सद्भिरुच्यते ॥ २३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
asiddhiḥ pāpakṛtyaṃ ca hiṃsā ceti prakīrtitāḥ |
etair doṣair vimukto yaḥ sa damaḥ sadbhir ucyate || 23 ||

lines.iast: asiddhiḥ pāpakṛtyaṃ ca hiṃsā ceti prakīrtitāḥ
lines.deva: असिद्धिः पापकृत्यं च हिंसा चेति प्रकीर्तिताः

lines.iast: etair doṣair vimukto yaḥ sa damaḥ sadbhir ucyate

padaccheda.iast: asiddhiḥ pāpa-kṛtyam ca hiṃsā ca iti prakīrtitāḥ etaiḥ doṣaiḥ vimuktaḥ yaḥ saḥ damaḥ sadbhiḥ ucyate
padaccheda.deva: असिद्धिः पाप-कृत्यम् च हिंसा च इति प्रकीर्तिताः एतैः दोषैः विमुक्तः यः सः दमः सद्भिः उच्यते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: failure, sinful deeds and injury: so they are declared. (The virtue) that is free from these faults is called restraint by the good.

notes: Śaṅkara: asiddhi: (the failure to attain) dharma, knowledge and dispassion. pāpakṛtya: doing what is forbidden. hiṃsā: injury not enjoined (by scripture). So the faults of restraint are declared. The virtue that is free from these faults, untruth and the rest, is called restraint by the good.

Śaṅkara's count of the eighteen (2.21–23): anṛta, paiśuna, tṛṣṇā, prātikūlya, tamas, arati, lokadveṣa, abhimāna, vivāda, prāṇipīḍana, parivāda, ativāda, paritāpa, akṣamā, adhṛti, asiddhi, pāpakṛtya, hiṃsā.

sanskrit.deva:
मदोऽष्टादशदोषः स्यात्त्यागो भवति षड्विधः ।
विपर्ययाः स्मृता एते दमदोषा उदाहृताः ॥ २४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
mado 'ṣṭādaśadoṣaḥ syāt tyāgo bhavati ṣaḍvidhaḥ |
viparyayāḥ smṛtā ete damadoṣā udāhṛtāḥ || 24 ||

lines.iast: mado 'ṣṭādaśadoṣaḥ syāt tyāgo bhavati ṣaḍvidhaḥ
viparyayāḥ smṛtā ete damadoṣā udāhṛtāḥ

padaccheda.iast: madaḥ aṣṭādaśa-doṣaḥ syāt tyāgaḥ bhavati ṣaṭ-vidhaḥ viparyayāḥ smṛtāḥ ete dama-doṣāḥ udāhṛtāḥ
padaccheda.deva: मदः अष्टादश-दोषः स्यात् त्यागः भवति षट्-विधः विपर्ययाः स्मृताः एते दम-दोषाः उदाहृताः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.
past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: Pride has eighteen faults, and renunciation is sixfold. These (eighteen), held (before) to be the faults of restraint, are held (to be) their opposites (truth and the rest), and are declared (the ‘faults’ of pride, what destroys it).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now he states the faults of pride.

Śaṅkara: pride has eighteen faults, and renunciation is sixfold. viparyayāḥ smṛtā ete: these, untruth down to injury, which were held to be the faults of restraint, are held as their opposites, in the form of truth and the rest, and are declared the faults of pride (madadoṣa), that is, the destroyers of pride: truth, absence of slander, absence of thirst, absence of hostility, absence of darkness, (contentment), absence of hatred of people, absence of arrogance, absence of quarrelling, not killing living beings, absence of censure, absence of excessive talk, absence of brooding, patience, firmness, attainment, absence of sinful deeds and non-injury.
The edition prints damadoṣā udāhṛtāḥ, kept; Śaṅkara's heading (‘the faults of pride’) and his gloss (madadoṣāḥ madanāśakarāḥ) read madadoṣā, as the common texts do (p. 253).
In the list of opposites (p. 254) the print has atamo'rati, where the opposite of arati (rati, contentment) is expected; given here as contentment.

sanskrit.deva:
श्रेयांस्तु षड्विधस्त्यागस्तृतीयस्तत्र दुष्करः ।
तेन दुःखं तरन्त्येव तस्मिंस्त्यक्ते जितं भवेत् ॥ २५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śreyāṃs tu ṣaḍvidhas tyāgas tṛtīyas tatra duṣkaraḥ |
tena duḥkhaṃ taranty eva tasmiṃs tyakte jitaṃ bhavet || 25 ||

lines.iast: śreyāṃs tu ṣaḍvidhas tyāgas tṛtīyas tatra duṣkaraḥ
tena duḥkhaṃ taranty eva tasmiṃs tyakte jitaṃ bhavet
lines.deva: तेन दुःखं तरन्त्येव तस्मिंस्त्यक्ते जितं भवेत्

padaccheda.iast: śreyān tu ṣaṭ-vidhaḥ tyāgaḥ tṛtīyaḥ tatra duṣkaraḥ tena duḥkham taranti eva tasmin tyakte jitam bhavet
padaccheda.deva: श्रेयान् तु षट्-विधः त्यागः तृतीयः तत्र दुष्करः तेन दुःखम् तरन्ति एव तस्मिन् त्यक्ते जितम् भवेत्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. loc. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: The sixfold renunciation is better; among these the third is hard to do. By it they cross sorrow indeed; when that (renunciation) is made, (all) is conquered.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: it was said ‘renunciation is sixfold’ (2.24); on this he says:

Śaṅkara: the sixfold renunciation is better; among these six renunciations the third is hard to do, hard to accomplish. By that third renunciation they cross sorrow, divided into the kinds that arise from oneself and the rest; when that renunciation is made, all is conquered.

sanskrit.deva:
अर्हते याचमानाय पुत्रान्वित्तं ददाति यत् ।
इष्टापूर्तं द्वितीयं स्यान्नित्यं वैराग्ययोगतः ॥ २६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
arhate yācamānāya putrān vittaṃ dadāti yat |
iṣṭāpūrtaṃ dvitīyaṃ syān nityaṃ vairāgyayogataḥ || 26 ||

lines.iast: arhate yācamānāya putrān vittaṃ dadāti yat
iṣṭāpūrtaṃ dvitīyaṃ syān nityaṃ vairāgyayogataḥ

padaccheda.iast: arhate yācamānāya putrān vittam dadāti yat iṣṭāpūrtam dvitīyam syāt nityam vairāgya-yogataḥ
padaccheda.deva: अर्हते याचमानाय पुत्रान् वित्तम् ददाति यत् इष्टापूर्तम् द्वितीयम् स्यात् नित्यम् वैराग्य-योगतः

translations.text: That one gives sons and wealth to a worthy man who asks (is the first pair of renunciations); sacrifices and works of merit would be the second; (the giving up of wealth and the rest) constantly, through dispassion,

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he now shows the six kinds of renunciation (tyāga) named in 2.24–25.

Śaṅkara: arhate: to one who is fit. Giving sons and wealth to a fit man who asks is a pair of renunciations, the first among the six. iṣṭa is giving in the rites of the Veda (śrauta), pūrta giving in the rites of the smṛti; some say iṣṭa is what is given to the gods, pūrta what is given to the ancestors: this pair is the second. nityaṃ vairāgyayogataḥ goes with the next verse: the giving up of wealth and the rest by one whose mind is pure and who, seeing in things the fault of impermanence and the rest, has turned from them, and the giving up of desire, together are the third.

sanskrit.deva:
कामत्यागश्च राजेन्द्र स तृतीय इति स्मृतः ।
अप्रमादी भवेदेतैः स चाप्यष्टगुणो मतः ॥ २७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kāmatyāgaś ca rājendra sa tṛtīya iti smṛtaḥ |
apramādī bhaved etaiḥ sa cāpy aṣṭaguṇo mataḥ || 27 ||

lines.iast: kāmatyāgaś ca rājendra sa tṛtīya iti smṛtaḥ
lines.deva: कामत्यागश्च राजेन्द्र स तृतीय इति स्मृतः

lines.iast: apramādī bhaved etaiḥ sa cāpy aṣṭaguṇo mataḥ

padaccheda.iast: kāma-tyāgaḥ ca rājendra saḥ tṛtīyaḥ iti smṛtaḥ apramādī bhavet etaiḥ saḥ ca api aṣṭa-guṇaḥ mataḥ
padaccheda.deva: काम-त्यागः च राजेन्द्र सः तृतीयः इति स्मृतः अप्रमादी भवेत् एतैः सः च अपि अष्ट-गुणः मतः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: and the renunciation of desire, O lord of kings: that is held to be the third. By these one becomes heedful; and that (heedfulness) too is considered to have eight qualities.

notes: Śaṅkara: the giving up of wealth and the rest out of dispassion (26) and the giving up of desire make the third pair. Asked what comes of these, he says: in the heedful desire perishes; he quotes the Rājadharma: ‘the stain of dharma is ill-will, the stain of wealth is hoarding; desire has heedfulness as its stain, and it increases good qualities further’. He who has these six renunciations becomes heedful; that heedfulness (sa = apramādaḥ) is joined with eight qualities, named in the next verse.

sanskrit.deva:
सत्यं ध्यानं समाधानं चोद्यं वैराग्यमेव च ।
अस्तेयो ब्रह्मचर्यं च तथासंग्रह एव च ॥ २८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
satyaṃ dhyānaṃ samādhānaṃ codyaṃ vairāgyam eva ca |
asteyo brahmacaryaṃ ca tathāsaṃgraha eva ca || 28 ||

lines.iast: satyaṃ dhyānaṃ samādhānaṃ codyaṃ vairāgyam eva ca
lines.deva: सत्यं ध्यानं समाधानं चोद्यं वैराग्यमेव च

lines.iast: asteyo brahmacaryaṃ ca tathāsaṃgraha eva ca
lines.deva: अस्तेयो ब्रह्मचर्यं च तथासंग्रह एव च

padaccheda.iast: satyam dhyānam samādhānam codyam vairāgyam eva ca asteyaḥ brahmacaryam ca tathā asaṃgrahaḥ eva ca
padaccheda.deva: सत्यम् ध्यानम् समाधानम् चोद्यम् वैराग्यम् एव च अस्तेयः ब्रह्मचर्यम् च तथा असंग्रहः एव च

translations.text: Truth, meditation, absorption, inquiry, and dispassion; not stealing, brahmacarya, and so too non-possession.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: what are those (eight qualities)? He shows them.

Śaṅkara: satya: speaking as things are. dhyāna: the flow of the mind upon some auspicious support, such as the Puruṣa in the orb (of the sun), unbroken like a stream of oil. samādhāna: having withdrawn Viśva and the rest by the praṇava, abiding as the non-dual Brahman, the Self, whose own nature is consciousness, being and bliss. codya: the questioning ‘who am I, whose, whence?’ and the like. vairāgya: freedom from thirst for objects seen and heard of (in the Veda). asteya: not stealing, either of the self or of goods; stealing the self is named in 1.33 (‘he who takes the self, which is one way, to be another’). brahmacarya: giving up the eightfold union, as it is said: ‘remembering, speaking of, play, looking, talk in secret, intention, resolve and the act itself: this the wise call the eightfold union; brahmacarya is the opposite, with these same eight marks’. asaṃgraha: not taking possession of sons, wife, fields and the rest. These one should keep.

sanskrit.deva:
एवं दोषा दमस्योक्तास्तान्दोषान्परिवर्जयेत् ।
दोषत्यागेऽप्रमादः स्यात्स चाप्यष्टगुणो मतः ॥ २९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
evaṃ doṣā damasyoktās tān doṣān parivarjayet |
doṣatyāge 'pramādaḥ syāt sa cāpy aṣṭaguṇo mataḥ || 29 ||

lines.iast: evaṃ doṣā damasyoktās tān doṣān parivarjayet
doṣatyāge 'pramādaḥ syāt sa cāpy aṣṭaguṇo mataḥ

padaccheda.iast: evam doṣāḥ damasya uktāḥ tān doṣān parivarjayet doṣa-tyāge apramādaḥ syāt saḥ ca api aṣṭa-guṇaḥ mataḥ
padaccheda.deva: एवम् दोषाः दमस्य उक्ताः तान् दोषान् परिवर्जयेत् दोष-त्यागे अप्रमादः स्यात् सः च अपि अष्ट-गुणः मतः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

words.meaning: when the faults are given up

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Thus the faults of self-restraint have been told; one should avoid those faults. When the faults are given up there would be heedfulness, and that too is considered to have eight qualities.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he says that one should avoid the faults.

Śaṅkara: the faults are those told at ‘self-restraint has eighteen faults’ (2.21–23). Why avoid them? Because when they are given up one will not be heedless. That heedfulness too has eight qualities, since they were named already at ‘truth, meditation’ (28).

sanskrit.deva:
सत्यात्मा भव राजेन्द्र सत्ये लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ।
तांस्तु सत्यमुखानाहुः सत्ये ह्यमृतमाहितम् ॥ ३० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
satyātmā bhava rājendra satye lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ |
tāṃs tu satyamukhān āhuḥ satye hy amṛtam āhitam || 30 ||

lines.iast: satyātmā bhava rājendra satye lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
lines.deva: सत्यात्मा भव राजेन्द्र सत्ये लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः

lines.iast: tāṃs tu satyamukhān āhuḥ satye hy amṛtam āhitam

padaccheda.iast: satya-ātmā bhava rājendra satye lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ tān tu satya-mukhān āhuḥ satye hi amṛtam āhitam
padaccheda.deva: सत्य-आत्मा भव राजेन्द्र सत्ये लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः तान् तु सत्य-मुखान् आहुः सत्ये हि अमृतम् आहितम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Be one whose very self is truth, O lord of kings; the worlds rest on truth. They call them ‘led by truth’; for in truth deathlessness (liberation) is placed.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now truth is praised.
Śaṅkara: satyātmā: whose own nature is truth. satyamukhān: having truth as the chief thing, gaining their own being in dependence on truth. amṛta: liberation.

sanskrit.deva:
निवृत्तेनैव दोषेण तपोव्रतमिहाचरेत् ।
एतद्धात्रा कृतं वित्तं सत्यमेव सतां वरम् ॥ ३१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nivṛttenaiva doṣeṇa tapovratam ihācaret |
etad dhātrā kṛtaṃ vittaṃ satyam eva satāṃ varam || 31 ||

lines.iast: nivṛttenaiva doṣeṇa tapovratam ihācaret
etad dhātrā kṛtaṃ vittaṃ satyam eva satāṃ varam
lines.deva: एतद्धात्रा कृतं वित्तं सत्यमेव सतां वरम्

padaccheda.iast: nivṛttena eva doṣeṇa tapaḥ-vratam iha ācaret etat dhātrā kṛtam vittam satyam eva satām varam
padaccheda.deva: निवृत्तेन एव दोषेण तपः-व्रतम् इह आचरेत् एतत् धात्रा कृतम् वित्तम् सत्यम् एव सताम् वरम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. ins. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: With every fault turned away, one should practise here the vow of austerity. This wealth made by the Creator (the supreme Lord), truth alone, is the best (wealth) of the good.

notes: Śaṅkara: nivṛttenaiva doṣeṇa: free of the faults told before at ‘anger and the rest’ (2.16). dhātrā: by the supreme Lord.

sanskrit.deva:
दोषैरेतैर्वियुक्तं तु गुणैरेतैः समन्वितम् ।
एतत्समृद्धमत्यर्थं तपो भवति केवलम् ॥ ३२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
doṣair etair viyuktaṃ tu guṇair etaiḥ samanvitam |
etat samṛddham atyarthaṃ tapo bhavati kevalam || 32 ||

lines.iast: doṣair etair viyuktaṃ tu guṇair etaiḥ samanvitam
etat samṛddham atyarthaṃ tapo bhavati kevalam

padaccheda.iast: doṣaiḥ etaiḥ viyuktam tu guṇaiḥ etaiḥ samanvitam etat samṛddham atyartham tapaḥ bhavati kevalam
padaccheda.deva: दोषैः एतैः वियुक्तम् तु गुणैः एतैः समन्वितम् एतत् समृद्धम् अत्यर्थम् तपः भवति केवलम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Freed from these faults and joined with these virtues, this becomes austerity exceedingly prosperous, unmixed.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now he concludes the matter begun with ‘how does austerity become exceedingly prosperous, unmixed?’ (2.11).
Śaṅkara: the faults are those told at ‘anger and the rest’ (2.16); the virtues are knowledge and the rest (2.19). On 2.12 he takes kevala as the seed (cause) of all this manifold.

sanskrit.deva:
यन्मां पृच्छसि राजेन्द्र संक्षेपात्तद्ब्रवीमि ते ।
एतत्पापहरं शुद्धं जन्ममृत्युजरापहम् ॥ ३३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yan māṃ pṛcchasi rājendra saṃkṣepāt tad bravīmi te |
etat pāpaharaṃ śuddhaṃ janmamṛtyujarāpaham || 33 ||

lines.iast: yan māṃ pṛcchasi rājendra saṃkṣepāt tad bravīmi te
etat pāpaharaṃ śuddhaṃ janmamṛtyujarāpaham

padaccheda.iast: yat mām pṛcchasi rājendra saṃkṣepāt tat bravīmi te etat pāpa-haram śuddham janma-mṛtyu-jarā-apaham
padaccheda.deva: यत् माम् पृच्छसि राजेन्द्र संक्षेपात् तत् ब्रवीमि ते एतत् पाप-हरम् शुद्धम् जन्म-मृत्यु-जरा-अपहम्

words.meaning: taking away birth, death and old age

translations.text: What you ask me, O lord of kings, that I tell you in brief. This (that is now to be told) removes sin, is pure, and takes away birth, death and old age.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: what need of more words?
Śaṅkara: saṃkṣepāt: in short. etat: what is about to be told.

sanskrit.deva:
इन्द्रियेभ्यश्च पञ्चभ्यो मनसश्चैव भारत ।
अतीतानागतेभ्यश्च मुक्तश्चेत्स सुखी भवेत् ॥ ३४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
indriyebhyaś ca pañcabhyo manasaś caiva bhārata |
atītānāgatebhyaś ca muktaś cet sa sukhī bhavet || 34 ||

lines.iast: indriyebhyaś ca pañcabhyo manasaś caiva bhārata
atītānāgatebhyaś ca muktaś cet sa sukhī bhavet

padaccheda.iast: indriyebhyaḥ ca pañcabhyaḥ manasaḥ ca eva bhārata atīta-anāgatebhyaḥ ca muktaḥ cet saḥ sukhī bhavet
padaccheda.deva: इन्द्रियेभ्यः च पञ्चभ्यः मनसः च एव भारत अतीत-अनागतेभ्यः च मुक्तः चेत् सः सुखी भवेत्

words.meaning: from the past and the future

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: If one is free from the five senses (with their objects, now present) and from the mind, O Bhārata, and from past and future (ones), he would be happy (and free).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: what is that? To this he says:
Śaṅkara: indriyebhyaḥ: from the five senses with their objects, those present; likewise from the past and the future. If one is free of them, he, being happy, is free indeed.

sanskrit.deva:
आख्यानपञ्चमैर्वेदैर्भूयिष्ठं कत्थ्यते जनः ।
तथा चान्ये चतुर्वेदास्त्रिवेदाश्च तथापरे ॥ ३५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ākhyānapañcamair vedair bhūyiṣṭhaṃ katthyate janaḥ |
tathā cānye caturvedās trivedāś ca tathāpare || 35 ||

lines.iast: ākhyānapañcamair vedair bhūyiṣṭhaṃ katthyate janaḥ
tathā cānye caturvedās trivedāś ca tathāpare

padaccheda.iast: ākhyāna-pañcamaiḥ vedaiḥ bhūyiṣṭham katthyate janaḥ tathā ca anye catuḥ-vedāḥ tri-vedāḥ ca tathā apare
padaccheda.deva: आख्यान-पञ्चमैः वेदैः भूयिष्ठम् कत्थ्यते जनः तथा च अन्ये चतुः-वेदाः त्रि-वेदाः च तथा अपरे

translations.text: A man prides himself greatly on the Vedas with the narratives as the fifth; so too others (are) men of four Vedas, and others again men of three Vedas,

notes: Śaṅkara: ākhyānapañcamāḥ: the Vedas whose fifth is the narrative, the Purāṇa; so the Chāndogya speaks of ‘the Itihāsa and Purāṇa as the fifth’ (7.1.2). By these Vedas a man thinks very highly of himself, ‘I am above all’ (katthyate = ślāghyate, bahumanyate).
Śaṅkara: some read kathyate: a man is called ‘one of five Vedas’ by the Vedas with the narratives as fifth.

sanskrit.deva:
द्विवेदाश्चैकवेदाश्च अनृचश्च तथापरे ।
एतेषु मेऽधिकं ब्रूहि यमहं वेद ब्राह्मणम् ॥ ३६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dvivedāś caikavedāś ca anṛcaś ca tathāpare |
eteṣu me 'dhikaṃ brūhi yam ahaṃ veda brāhmaṇam || 36 ||

lines.iast: dvivedāś caikavedāś ca anṛcaś ca tathāpare
eteṣu me 'dhikaṃ brūhi yam ahaṃ veda brāhmaṇam
lines.deva: एतेषु मेऽधिकं ब्रूहि यमहं वेद ब्राह्मणम्

padaccheda.iast: dvi-vedāḥ ca eka-vedāḥ ca anṛcaḥ ca tathā apare eteṣu me adhikam brūhi yam aham veda brāhmaṇam
padaccheda.deva: द्वि-वेदाः च एक-वेदाः च अनृचः च तथा अपरे एतेषु मे अधिकम् ब्रूहि यम् अहम् वेद ब्राह्मणम्

translations.text: men of two Vedas and of one Veda, and others again without the Ṛk. Tell me who among these is the greater, whom I may know as a brāhmaṇa.

notes: Śaṅkara: anṛcaḥ: others, who have given up the Ṛk and the other Vedas. eteṣu: among these men; adhikam: the best; veda: vidyām, I may know.

sanskrit.deva:
एकवेदस्य चाज्ञानाद्वेदास्ते बहवोऽभवन् ।
सत्यस्यैकस्य राजेन्द्र सत्ये कश्चिदवस्थितः ॥ ३७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ekavedasya cājñānād vedās te bahavo 'bhavan |
satyasyaikasya rājendra satye kaścid avasthitaḥ || 37 ||

lines.iast: ekavedasya cājñānād vedās te bahavo 'bhavan
satyasyaikasya rājendra satye kaścid avasthitaḥ

padaccheda.iast: eka-vedasya ca ajñānāt vedāḥ te bahavaḥ abhavan satyasya ekasya rājendra satye kaścit avasthitaḥ
padaccheda.deva: एक-वेदस्य च अज्ञानात् वेदाः ते बहवः अभवन् सत्यस्य एकस्य राजेन्द्र सत्ये कश्चित् अवस्थितः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: From not knowing the one Veda, (Brahman,) the Vedas came to be many: (from not knowing) the one True, O lord of kings. (Only) some one stands in the True.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: to show that he alone is a brāhmaṇa who abides as the non-dual Brahman, the Self, whose own nature is consciousness, being and bliss, he first shows that all else is rooted in not knowing that.

Śaṅkara: ekavedasya: of the one Veda: the knowable has the form ‘this’, (knowing) is not of the form ‘this’; vedana, knowing, is the Veda: so ‘of the one, the non-dual, whose form is consciousness’. From not understanding that one Veda, Brahman, the Ṛk and the other Vedas became many. They inquire into it in order to make it understood, and so gained the name Veda. Or they are Vedas because they establish what is (sadbhāva); or because they are the means of knowing; or because by them one gains oneself as dependent on Brahman; or because they are the cause of gaining Brahman as the Self: they are called Vedas because they bear on the senses of the roots vid ‘to consider’, vid ‘to be’, vid ‘to know’ and vid (vidḷ) ‘to gain’.

Śaṅkara: what is the one Veda? ‘Brahman is truth, knowledge, the infinite’ (Taittirīya 2.1). So from not understanding the True, Brahman, the one Veda, the Vedas were expounded as many: all of them are means to seeing its meaning. ‘O king, have you too, knowing this, come to stand in the True, Brahman?’ And: only some one is established in the True.

sanskrit.deva:
य एनं वेद तत्सत्यं प्राज्ञो भवति नित्यदा ।
दानमध्ययनं यज्ञो लोभादेव प्रवर्तते ॥ ३८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ya enaṃ veda tat satyaṃ prājño bhavati nityadā |
dānam adhyayanaṃ yajño lobhād eva pravartate || 38 ||

lines.iast: ya enaṃ veda tat satyaṃ prājño bhavati nityadā
lines.deva: य एनं वेद तत्सत्यं प्राज्ञो भवति नित्यदा

lines.iast: dānam adhyayanaṃ yajño lobhād eva pravartate

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ enam veda tat satyam prājñaḥ bhavati nityadā dānam adhyayanam yajñaḥ lobhāt eva pravartate
padaccheda.deva: यः एनम् वेद तत् सत्यम् प्राज्ञः भवति नित्यदा दानम् अध्ययनम् यज्ञः लोभात् एव प्रवर्तते

translations.text: He who knows this, that True, becomes wise for ever. (Of him who does not,) giving, study and sacrifice go on from greed alone.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: hear me further. He gives no gloss on the verse itself, and introduces the next: ‘Why? If one does not (know the True), hear what happens then.’

sanskrit.deva:
सत्यात्प्रच्यवमानानां संकल्पा वितथाभवन् ।
ततः कर्म प्रतायेत सत्यस्यानवधारणात् ॥ ३९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
satyāt pracyavamānānāṃ saṃkalpā vitathābhavan |
tataḥ karma pratāyeta satyasyānavadhāraṇāt || 39 ||

lines.iast: satyāt pracyavamānānāṃ saṃkalpā vitathābhavan
tataḥ karma pratāyeta satyasyānavadhāraṇāt

padaccheda.iast: satyāt pracyavamānānām saṃkalpāḥ vitathāḥ abhavan tataḥ karma pratāyeta satyasya anavadhāraṇāt
padaccheda.deva: सत्यात् प्रच्यवमानानाम् संकल्पाः वितथाः अभवन् ततः कर्म प्रतायेत सत्यस्य अनवधारणात्

translations.text: The resolves of those who fall from the True became vain; then action is spread out, from not ascertaining the True.

notes: Śaṅkara: satyāt: from Brahman, marked by truth, knowledge and the rest. Those who fall from it, giving up their natural being as Brahman and taking the non-self, the body and the rest, as the self: their resolves become vain, that is, their natural true resolve and the rest do not come about. Then action, sacrifice and the rest, is spread out. All this comes from not understanding the True, Brahman marked by truth and the rest, since saṃsāra is caused by ignorance of the Self: so long as one does not know the supreme Self directly as oneself, he, overcome by the three afflictions, dragged this way and that by passion and the rest as by crocodiles, deluded again and again, with resolves that are not true, busies himself with means to heaven, cattle, food and the like, which are all to be given up.

sanskrit.deva:
विद्याद्बहुपठं तं तु बहुवागिति ब्राह्मणम् ।
य एव सत्यान्नापैति स ज्ञेयो ब्राह्मणस्त्वया ॥ ४० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vidyād bahupaṭhaṃ taṃ tu bahuvāg iti brāhmaṇam |
ya eva satyān nāpaiti sa jñeyo brāhmaṇas tvayā || 40 ||

lines.iast: vidyād bahupaṭhaṃ taṃ tu bahuvāg iti brāhmaṇam
ya eva satyān nāpaiti sa jñeyo brāhmaṇas tvayā
lines.deva: य एव सत्यान्नापैति स ज्ञेयो ब्राह्मणस्त्वया

padaccheda.iast: vidyāt bahu-paṭham tam tu bahu-vāk iti brāhmaṇam yaḥ eva satyāt na apaiti saḥ jñeyaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ tvayā
padaccheda.deva: विद्यात् बहु-पठम् तम् तु बहु-वाक् इति ब्राह्मणम् यः एव सत्यात् न अपैति सः ज्ञेयः ब्राह्मणः त्वया

translations.text: One should know him who reads much as ‘a man of many words’, (not) as a brāhmaṇa. He who does not depart from the True: he is to be known by you as a brāhmaṇa.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now he gives the mark of a brāhmaṇa.

Śaṅkara: bahupaṭham: him who studies the Vedas with the narratives as fifth one should know as a man of many words, not as a brāhmaṇa in truth. Who then is the brāhmaṇa in the chief sense? He who does not depart from the True, marked by truth and the rest, who abides as the non-dual Brahman, the Self, whose own nature is consciousness, being and bliss: him alone you should know as a brāhmaṇa, not the other, who, fallen from the True and with his end not gained, engages in action. So the śruti shows that the knower of Brahman alone is a brāhmaṇa: ‘having done with silence and non-silence, then he is a brāhmaṇa’ (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.5.1), and ‘free of sin, free of stain, free of doubt, he becomes a brāhmaṇa’ (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.23).

sanskrit.deva:
छन्दांसि नाम द्विपदां वरिष्ठ स्वच्छन्दयोगेन भवन्ति तत्र ।
छन्दोविदस्तेन च तानधीत्य गता हि वेदस्य न वेद्यमार्याः ॥ ४१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
chandāṃsi nāma dvipadāṃ variṣṭha svacchandayogena bhavanti tatra |
chandovidas tena ca tān adhītya gatā hi vedasya na vedyam āryāḥ || 41 ||

lines.iast: chandāṃsi nāma dvipadāṃ variṣṭha svacchandayogena bhavanti tatra
lines.deva: छन्दांसि नाम द्विपदां वरिष्ठ स्वच्छन्दयोगेन भवन्ति तत्र

lines.iast: chandovidas tena ca tān adhītya gatā hi vedasya na vedyam āryāḥ
lines.deva: छन्दोविदस्तेन च तानधीत्य गता हि वेदस्य न वेद्यमार्याः

padaccheda.iast: chandāṃsi nāma dvipadām variṣṭha sva-chanda-yogena bhavanti tatra chandaḥ-vidaḥ tena ca tān adhītya gatāḥ hi vedasya na vedyam āryāḥ
padaccheda.deva: छन्दांसि नाम द्विपदाम् वरिष्ठ स्व-छन्द-योगेन भवन्ति तत्र छन्दः-विदः तेन च तान् अधीत्य गताः हि वेदस्य न वेद्यम् आर्याः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: The Vedas, O best of men, are of their own accord (a valid means of knowledge) there (in the supreme Self). And therefore the noble knowers of the Vedas, having studied them, have reached (the nature) of the Veda (the supreme Self), not the knowable.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: ‘If it were so, Brahman would be established; but it is not, for the Veda is about something else.’ To this he says:

Śaṅkara: chandāṃsi: the Vedas. svacchandayogena: svacchandatā is independence, as they will. tatra: in the supreme Self; there alone they are a valid means of knowledge. So the śruti: ‘the word that all the Vedas declare’ (Kaṭha 1.2.15), and ‘by all the Vedas I alone am to be known’ (Gītā 15.15). For the Veda ends in the goal of man, and all else, pierced by impermanence, impurity and sorrow, is no goal of man; so the Vedas are valid in teaching its nature, the knowledge of it and the means to that.

Śaṅkara: because the Vedas are of their own accord valid there, in the supreme Self, therefore the noble, the learned, the knowers of Brahman, having studied the Vedas, that is, having heard the Vedānta and the rest, have reached the nature of the Veda, the supreme Self whose form is consciousness, not the knowable, the manifold world.

sanskrit.deva:
न वेदानां वेदिता कश्चिदस्ति वेदेन वेदं न विदुर्न वेद्यम् ।
यो वेद वेदं स च वेद वेद्यं यो वेद वेद्यं न स वेद सत्यम् ॥ ४२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na vedānāṃ veditā kaścid asti vedena vedaṃ na vidur na vedyam |
yo veda vedaṃ sa ca veda vedyaṃ yo veda vedyaṃ na sa veda satyam || 42 ||

lines.iast: na vedānāṃ veditā kaścid asti vedena vedaṃ na vidur na vedyam
lines.deva: न वेदानां वेदिता कश्चिदस्ति वेदेन वेदं न विदुर्न वेद्यम्

lines.iast: yo veda vedaṃ sa ca veda vedyaṃ yo veda vedyaṃ na sa veda satyam
lines.deva: यो वेद वेदं स च वेद वेद्यं यो वेद वेद्यं न स वेद सत्यम्

padaccheda.iast: na vedānām veditā kaścit asti vedena vedam na viduḥ na vedyam yaḥ veda vedam saḥ ca veda vedyam yaḥ veda vedyam na saḥ veda satyam
padaccheda.deva: न वेदानाम् वेदिता कश्चित् अस्ति वेदेन वेदम् न विदुः न वेद्यम् यः वेद वेदम् सः च वेद वेद्यम् यः वेद वेद्यम् न सः वेद सत्यम्

translations.text: None of the Vedas is the knower (of the supreme Self). By the Veda (Ṛk and the rest) they do not know the Veda (the supreme Self whose form is consciousness), nor the knowable. He who knows the Veda knows the knowable too; he who knows the knowable does not know the True.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: ‘If it is known by the Veda, that would conflict with śrutis such as “other than the known, and above the unknown” (Kena 1.4) and “whence words turn back, not reaching it, with the mind” (Taittirīya 2.4).’ To this doubt he says:

Śaṅkara: among the Vedas, the Ṛk and the rest, not one is the knower of the supreme Self, which is beyond the reach of words and whose form is consciousness. Why? Because by the Veda in the form of the Ṛk and the rest, which is insentient, they do not know the Veda, the supreme Self whose form is consciousness; nor do they know the knowable, the manifold, since everything is established only in dependence on consciousness. Because of that, he who knows the Veda, the supreme Self whose form is consciousness, knows the knowable too, all this; so the śruti: ‘by the seeing, hearing, thinking and knowing of the Self all this is known’ (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.4.5). He who knows the knowable as a form does not know the True, the supreme Self marked by truth and the rest.

sanskrit.deva:
यो वेद वेदान्स च वेद वेद्यं न तं विदुर्वेदविदो न वेदाः ।
तथापि वेदेन विदन्ति वेदं ये ब्राह्मणा वेदविदो भवन्ति ॥ ४३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yo veda vedān sa ca veda vedyaṃ na taṃ vidur vedavido na vedāḥ |
tathāpi vedena vidanti vedaṃ ye brāhmaṇā vedavido bhavanti || 43 ||

lines.iast: yo veda vedān sa ca veda vedyaṃ na taṃ vidur vedavido na vedāḥ
lines.deva: यो वेद वेदान्स च वेद वेद्यं न तं विदुर्वेदविदो न वेदाः

lines.iast: tathāpi vedena vidanti vedaṃ ye brāhmaṇā vedavido bhavanti
lines.deva: तथापि वेदेन विदन्ति वेदं ये ब्राह्मणा वेदविदो भवन्ति

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ veda vedān saḥ ca veda vedyam na tam viduḥ veda-vidaḥ na vedāḥ tathāpi vedena vidanti vedam ye brāhmaṇāḥ veda-vidaḥ bhavanti
padaccheda.deva: यः वेद वेदान् सः च वेद वेद्यम् न तम् विदुः वेद-विदः न वेदाः तथापि वेदेन विदन्ति वेदम् ये ब्राह्मणाः वेद-विदः भवन्ति

translations.text: He who knows the Vedas (the Ṛk and the rest) knows the knowable (only). The knowers of the Veda do not know Him, nor do the Vedas. Even so, by the Veda they know the Veda (the supreme Self): those brāhmaṇas who are knowers of the Veda (who know how the Vedas teach).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: ‘Then, in saying “by the Veda they know neither the Veda nor the knowable”, it is said that for one who does not know the Self the manifold is not established at all.’ To this doubt he says:

Śaṅkara: he who knows the Vedas, the Ṛk and the rest, he too, not knowing the Self, knows the knowable, the manifold, by a knowing distinct from it. Then would he know the supreme Self too, like the knowable? No: the knowers of the Veda do not know Him, who is beyond the reach of words; nor do the Vedas: they do not make Him their object. Then how is Brahman taught in the Upaniṣads? Though Brahman is not the object of speech and the rest, still by the Veda, the Ṛk and the rest, they know the Veda, the supreme Self whose form is consciousness. Who? Those brāhmaṇas who are knowers of the Veda, who know the way in which the Vedas teach the Veda.

sanskrit.deva:
यामांशभागस्य तथा हि वेदा यथा हि शाखा च महीरुहस्य ।
संवेदनेऽप्येवमथामनन्ति तस्मिन्हि नित्ये परमात्मनोऽर्थे ॥ ४४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yāmāṃśabhāgasya tathā hi vedā yathā hi śākhā ca mahīruhasya |
saṃvedane 'py evam athāmananti tasmin hi nitye paramātmano 'rthe || 44 ||

lines.iast: yāmāṃśabhāgasya tathā hi vedā yathā hi śākhā ca mahīruhasya
lines.deva: यामांशभागस्य तथा हि वेदा यथा हि शाखा च महीरुहस्य

lines.iast: saṃvedane 'py evam athāmananti tasmin hi nitye paramātmano 'rthe

padaccheda.iast: yāma-aṃśa-bhāgasya tathā hi vedāḥ yathā hi śākhā ca mahīruhasya saṃvedane api evam atha āmananti tasmin hi nitye parama-ātmanaḥ arthe
padaccheda.deva: याम-अंश-भागस्य तथा हि वेदाः यथा हि शाखा च महीरुहस्य संवेदने अपि एवम् अथ आमनन्ति तस्मिन् हि नित्ये परम-आत्मनः अर्थे

words.meaning: of the part of the moon's portion

translations.text: As the branch of a tree (is a means to seeing) the part of the moon's portion, so indeed are the Vedas (a means) for the consciousness of the supreme Self, for that eternal object: so they declare.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: how then do the Vedas teach Brahman, which is no object at all?

Śaṅkara: yāmāṃśabhāgasya: of the part of the moon's portion, yāma standing for the moon by the śruti ‘the moon is triyāma’. As, in seeing the digit of the moon on the first day of the bright fortnight, the branch of a tree is the means, so the Vedas are means to the consciousness that is the very nature of the supreme Self, to the eternal, imperishable object (artha) that is the highest goal of man, whose form is full bliss; they do not teach directly the supreme Self, which is beyond the reach of words: so (the knowers) declare.

sanskrit.deva:
अभिजानामि ब्राह्मणमाख्यातारं विचक्षणम् ।
एवं योऽभिविजानाति स जानाति परं हि तत् ॥ ४५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
abhijānāmi brāhmaṇam ākhyātāraṃ vicakṣaṇam |
evaṃ yo 'bhivijānāti sa jānāti paraṃ hi tat || 45 ||

lines.iast: abhijānāmi brāhmaṇam ākhyātāraṃ vicakṣaṇam
evaṃ yo 'bhivijānāti sa jānāti paraṃ hi tat
lines.deva: एवं योऽभिविजानाति स जानाति परं हि तत्

padaccheda.iast: abhijānāmi brāhmaṇam ākhyātāram vicakṣaṇam evam yaḥ abhivijānāti saḥ jānāti param hi tat
padaccheda.deva: अभिजानामि ब्राह्मणम् आख्यातारम् विचक्षणम् एवम् यः अभिविजानाति सः जानाति परम् हि तत्

translations.text: I recognize as a brāhmaṇa the discerning expounder (of the way the Vedas teach). He who knows this thoroughly knows that supreme (Brahman).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he who, having understood the way in which the Vedas teach the Self whose form is the Veda, explains it: he too is a brāhmaṇa.

Śaṅkara: I recognize as a brāhmaṇa the discerning expounder who explains the way the Veda teaches. Objection: the śruti calls him a brāhmaṇa who abides having done with learning, childlikeness and the rest (‘then he is a brāhmaṇa’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.5.1); how then is it said, ‘I recognize as a brāhmaṇa the expounder’? Answer: he who thoroughly knows the way, told by me, in which the Vedas teach the Self whose form is knowing, knows that supreme Brahman. For he who abides having done with learning soon does with childlikeness and the rest, and becomes a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit.deva:
नास्य पर्येषणं गच्छेत्प्रत्यर्थिषु कदाचन ।
अविचिन्वन्निमं वेदे ततः पश्यति तं प्रभुम् ॥ ४६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nāsya paryeṣaṇaṃ gacchet pratyarthiṣu kadācana |
avicinvann imaṃ vede tataḥ paśyati taṃ prabhum || 46 ||

lines.iast: nāsya paryeṣaṇaṃ gacchet pratyarthiṣu kadācana
avicinvann imaṃ vede tataḥ paśyati taṃ prabhum
lines.deva: अविचिन्वन्निमं वेदे ततः पश्यति तं प्रभुम्

padaccheda.iast: na asya paryeṣaṇam gacchet pratyarthiṣu kadācana avicinvan imam vede tataḥ paśyati tam prabhum
padaccheda.deva: न अस्य पर्येषणम् गच्छेत् प्रत्यर्थिषु कदाचन अविचिन्वन् इमम् वेदे ततः पश्यति तम् प्रभुम्

translations.text: One should never go searching (for the Self) among its adversaries. Not gathering (objects), (seeking) this (inner Self) in the Veda, he then sees that Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: because only one devoted to the True is known as a brāhmaṇa, one should not be given to objects.

Śaṅkara: in the light of the verse ‘objects, the senses, the body and the ego are the fierce enemies of the yogin, outer and inner’, one should not go searching about (pari-eṣaṇa) among the adversaries of this self, the body, the senses and their objects such as sound; that is, one should not be bent on seeking objects. avicinvan: not amassing objects; imam: this inner Self, in the Veda, in the Upaniṣads, in sentences such as ‘that thou art’; then, afterwards, he sees that Lord, the supreme Self: he knows Him as the Self.

Śaṅkara, a second explanation: one should not search for the self (asya) in its adversaries, the body, the senses and the rest, that is, should not take the body, the senses and their properties as the self. Not gathering them as the self, taking the witness of them alone as the Self, after the meanings of the words ‘that’ and ‘thou’ have been purified, he sees this supreme Self, the witness of the knower and the rest: not taking body, senses and their properties as the self, he sees by sentences such as ‘that thou art’ the supreme Self as the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
तूष्णींभूत उपासीत न चेच्छेन्मनसा अपि ।
अभ्यावर्तेत ब्रह्मास्मै बह्वनन्तरमाप्नुयात् ॥ ४७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tūṣṇīṃbhūta upāsīta na cecchen manasā api |
abhyāvarteta brahmāsmai bahv anantaram āpnuyāt || 47 ||

lines.iast: tūṣṇīṃbhūta upāsīta na cecchen manasā api
abhyāvarteta brahmāsmai bahv anantaram āpnuyāt

padaccheda.iast: tūṣṇīm-bhūtaḥ upāsīta na ca icchet manasā api abhyāvarteta brahma asmai bahu anantaram āpnuyāt
padaccheda.deva: तूष्णीम्-भूतः उपासीत न च इच्छेत् मनसा अपि अभ्यावर्तेत ब्रह्म अस्मै बहु अनन्तरम् आप्नुयात्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Become silent, one should worship (one's own Self), and not desire (objects) even with the mind. Brahman would turn towards him; thereupon he would reach the much (the plenitude, the supreme Self).

notes: Śaṅkara: because the seeing of the Self comes about only by giving up all objects, therefore, become silent, having renounced all works, having given up all but one's own Self, become alone, one should worship one's own Self alone as the world; and should not desire even with the mind: should make no desire for objects. To him, the brāhmaṇa who, become silent, has withdrawn from objects and worships his own Self as the world, Brahman, marked as ‘without before’ and the rest (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.5.19), would turn towards him, would come face to face. So the śruti: ‘whom he chooses, by him he is gained; to him this Self reveals its own form’ (Kaṭha 1.2.23). Thereupon, his own form made manifest, he would reach the much (bahu), the plenitude (bhūman), the supreme Self beyond darkness.

sanskrit.deva:
मौनाद्धि मुनिर्भवति नारण्यवसनान्मुनिः ।
अक्षरं तं तु यो वेद स मुनिश्रेष्ठ उच्यते ॥ ४८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
maunād dhi munir bhavati nāraṇyavasanān muniḥ |
akṣaraṃ taṃ tu yo veda sa muniśreṣṭha ucyate || 48 ||

lines.iast: maunād dhi munir bhavati nāraṇyavasanān muniḥ
akṣaraṃ taṃ tu yo veda sa muniśreṣṭha ucyate
lines.deva: अक्षरं तं तु यो वेद स मुनिश्रेष्ठ उच्यते

padaccheda.iast: maunāt hi muniḥ bhavati na araṇya-vasanāt muniḥ akṣaram tam tu yaḥ veda saḥ muni-śreṣṭhaḥ ucyate
padaccheda.deva: मौनात् हि मुनिः भवति न अरण्य-वसनात् मुनिः अक्षरम् तम् तु यः वेद सः मुनि-श्रेष्ठः उच्यते

translations.text: By silence indeed one becomes a sage, not by dwelling in the forest. But he who knows that imperishable (supreme Self) is called the best of sages.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he alone is a muni too.

Śaṅkara: maunāt: by the being silent told before (47), not merely by dwelling in the forest, does one become a sage. Among those who have become silent, he who knows that imperishable, the supreme Self, directly as ‘I am this’, is called the best of sages. So the śruti: ‘knowing this very one he becomes a sage’ (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.22). akṣaraṃ tam: ‘that imperishable, the supreme Self’ (masculine tam by the sense).
The edition: the reading sa (‘he’) in the second half is doubtful in the print; the transcript's reading is kept.

sanskrit.deva:
सर्वार्थानां व्याकरणाद्वैयाकरण उच्यते ।
तन्मूलतो व्याकरणं व्याकरोतीति तत्तथा ॥ ४९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sarvārthānāṃ vyākaraṇād vaiyākaraṇa ucyate |
tanmūlato vyākaraṇaṃ vyākarotīti tat tathā || 49 ||

lines.iast: sarvārthānāṃ vyākaraṇād vaiyākaraṇa ucyate
tanmūlato vyākaraṇaṃ vyākarotīti tat tathā

padaccheda.iast: sarva-arthānām vyākaraṇāt vaiyākaraṇaḥ ucyate tat-mūlataḥ vyākaraṇam vyākaroti iti tat tathā
padaccheda.deva: सर्व-अर्थानाम् व्याकरणात् वैयाकरणः उच्यते तत्-मूलतः व्याकरणम् व्याकरोति इति तत् तथा

translations.text: One is called a ‘grammarian’ (vaiyākaraṇa) from making distinct all things. From that (the Imperishable) as the root is the making distinct (of name and form); he (the knower) makes that (Brahman) distinct in that way: so (he is a grammarian).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he alone is a grammarian too.

Śaṅkara: one is called a grammarian (vaiyākaraṇa) from making distinct (vyākaraṇa) all things, not from analysing some part of words. Granted; what follows? tanmūlato vyākaraṇam: from the Imperishable named before (48) comes the making distinct of the whole manifold of name and form; so the śruti: ‘entering with this living self, let me make distinct name and form’ (Chāndogya 6.3.2). Hence Brahman alone is directly the ‘grammarian’. vyākarotīti tat tathā: this knower too makes that Brahman distinct in just that way, and so is a grammarian.

sanskrit.deva:
प्रत्यक्षदर्शी लोकानां सर्वदर्शी भवेन्नरः ।
सत्ये वै ब्रह्मणि तिष्ठंस्तद्विद्वान्सर्वविद्भवेत् ॥ ५० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
pratyakṣadarśī lokānāṃ sarvadarśī bhaven naraḥ |
satye vai brahmaṇi tiṣṭhaṃs tad vidvān sarvavid bhavet || 50 ||

lines.iast: pratyakṣadarśī lokānāṃ sarvadarśī bhaven naraḥ
satye vai brahmaṇi tiṣṭhaṃs tad vidvān sarvavid bhavet

padaccheda.iast: pratyakṣa-darśī lokānām sarva-darśī bhavet naraḥ satye vai brahmaṇi tiṣṭhan tat vidvān sarva-vit bhavet
padaccheda.deva: प्रत्यक्ष-दर्शी लोकानाम् सर्व-दर्शी भवेत् नरः सत्ये वै ब्रह्मणि तिष्ठन् तत् विद्वान् सर्व-वित् भवेत्

translations.text: The man who sees the worlds directly would be ‘all-seeing’ (only if he sees the supreme Self, which is all). Abiding in the True, in Brahman, knowing That (as the Self), he would be all-knowing.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he alone is all-knowing too.

Śaṅkara: he who sees directly the worlds, Bhūḥ and the rest, would be the all-seeing man: he sees the supreme Self whose form is all. And he, abiding in the True, in Brahman marked by truth and the rest, fixes his mind there; knowing that Brahman as the Self, he becomes all-knowing, knows all. So he alone is directly omniscient, not one who sees only the non-self.

sanskrit.deva:
ज्ञानादिषु स्थितोऽप्येवं क्षत्रिय ब्रह्म पश्यति ।
वेदानां चारपूर्वेण चैतद्विद्वन्ब्रवीमि ते ॥ ५१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
jñānādiṣu sthito 'py evaṃ kṣatriya brahma paśyati |
vedānāṃ cārapūrveṇa caitad vidvan bravīmi te || 51 ||

lines.iast: jñānādiṣu sthito 'py evaṃ kṣatriya brahma paśyati
vedānāṃ cārapūrveṇa caitad vidvan bravīmi te

padaccheda.iast: jñāna-ādiṣu sthitaḥ api evam kṣatriya brahma paśyati vedānām cāra-pūrveṇa ca etat vidvan bravīmi te
padaccheda.deva: ज्ञान-आदिषु स्थितः अपि एवम् क्षत्रिय ब्रह्म पश्यति वेदानाम् चार-पूर्वेण च एतत् विद्वन् ब्रवीमि ते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Abiding in knowledge and the rest too, O warrior, one sees Brahman in this way, by first going through the Vedas (by first hearing the Vedānta); and this, O learned one, I tell you.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: the sense told at ‘he who does not leave these (twelve)’ (2.20) he shows again, to show that it must be done.

Śaṅkara: jñānādiṣu: in knowledge and the rest, told before at ‘knowledge and truth’ (2.19); abiding in them too, one sees Brahman in the same way as one abiding in the True sees Brahman (50). vedānāṃ cārapūrveṇa: preceded by the hearing of the Vedānta.

Śaṅkara, a second explanation: this lays down a further quality. Even abiding in knowledge and the rest, one does not see Brahman by that alone, but sees it only in the way about to be told, preceded by inquiry into the Vedānta, by hearing the Vedānta and the rest. etat: this manner of inquiring into the Vedānta, O learned one, I tell you, that is, I shall tell you.
